The API level contains the business logic of an application: the rules by which users can interact with the application’s services, data, or functions. Since the API or service level directly affects the data layer and the presentation layer, this is the ideal point for continuous testing for quality control and development teams. Although traditional testing has focused on the user interface, the benefits of API testing are becoming increasingly known. Although there are many aspects of API testing, it is usually necessary to make requests to one or sometimes multiple API endpoints and review the response, either for performance or security reasons, functional fixes, or simply a status check. While the UI test may focus on verifying the appearance of a web interface or on the operation of a specific payment button, the API test places much more emphasis on testing business logic, data and security responses, and performance bottlenecks. What is API Testing? The API test is a type of software test in which the API (Application Programming Interface) is tested directly and as part of the integration test to determine whether they meet expectations in terms of functionality, reliability, and reliability. APIs do not have a graphical user interface; API tests are performed at the message level. API tests are now considered critical for test automation, as APIs are now the primary interface for application logic and GUI tests with release cycles are difficult to maintain Types of tests can be performed in API tests: Functional test – to check if the API works and does exactly what it needs to do Reliability test – to check if the API can be connected and produces consistent results consistently Validation Test- Allows you to examine aspects related to the product, behavior, and efficiency of an API Load test – performed to ensure API performance in normal and peak conditions UI Test- involves testing the UI for the API and other integral parts Security test- to check if the API is protected from all possible external threats Penetration test- to identify vulnerabilities in an application from the perspective of an attacker Fuzz test – to test the API against the limits to prepare the “worst-case scenarios.” Challenges of API Testing There is no graphical interface that makes it difficult for testers to provide input values Managing test cases is difficult because a tester may have to manage millions of test cases The tester must have experience in API-controlled programming languages It takes time, takes a lot of time and resources to develop design tools and tests Inadequate documentation makes it difficult for a test designer to understand the purpose of old.content: Skip to content Home > Data Science For a Non-Technical Background Data Science For a Non-Technical Background From non-technical to data scientist: A comprehensive guide to learning data science skills, building a portfolio, and starting your new career with 3RI Technologies Table of Contents PriyankaS3ri May 19, 2025 2:44 pm The demand for data science professionals has grown rapidly across industries such as healthcare, finance, e-commerce, marketing, logistics, and IT services. Businesses today rely heavily on data to make decisions, improve customer experience, and predict future trends. Because of this shift, many students and working professionals from non-technical backgrounds are now exploring – Data science coourse in Pune. One of the most common questions beginners ask is: Can a non-technical person learn data science? The answer is yes. Modern learning platforms, structured mentorship, beginner-friendly tools, and practical training have made data science more accessible than ever before. Whether you come from commerce, arts, management, mechanical engineering, or another non-IT background, you can gradually build the required skills with the right roadmap and guidance. This guide explains everything you need to know about learning data science from a non-technical background, including skills, career paths, learning roadmap, challenges, and training opportunities in Pune. Can a Non-Technical Person Learn Data Science? Many learners assume data science is only for programmers or computer science graduates. In reality, companies today value analytical thinking, business understanding, communication skills, and problem-solving abilities just as much as coding knowledge. A non-technical learner may initially find programming and statistics unfamiliar, but these concepts can be learned step-by-step through proper training and practice. Why Data Science Is No Longer Limited to IT Professionals Earlier, data-related roles were highly technical and mostly handled by software engineers. Today, businesses need professionals who can interpret data and convert it into meaningful business insights. This has opened opportunities for learners from various educational backgrounds. Industries hiring data professionals now include: Banking and finance Healthcare Retail and e-commerce Digital marketing Manufacturing Education Logistics and supply chain Professionals with domain knowledge often have an advantage because they understand industry-specific problems. Common Myths about Data science for Non-Technical Myth 1: “I need advanced coding skills.”Most beginner-level data science courses start with basic programming concepts and gradually move to advanced topics. Myth 2: “Mathematics needs to be extremely strong.” You need foundational statistics and logical thinking, not advanced theoretical mathematics. Myth 3: “Only engineers can become data scientists.” Many successful data professionals come from commerce, economics, business, and science backgrounds. Myth 4: “It is too late to switch careers.” Career transition into analytics and data science is now common among working professionals. Your Roadmap to a Successful Career in Data Science Data science has been one of the most sought after areas for over a decade, and it doesn’t seem to be slowing down. According to US Bureau of Labor Statistics projections, 11.5 million Data science jobs will exist by 2026.As of early 2024, there are only 4 million available data scientists’ specialist. This graphic illustrates the notable disparity between the number of data scientists needed and those that are available. Role Primary Responsibility Beginner Friendly Data Analyst Analyze reports and dashboards Yes Business Analyst Improve business decisions using data Yes Data Scientist Build predictive models and analytics systems Moderate Machine Learning Engineer Develop AI-driven applications Advanced Data Engineer Manage data infrastructure Technical Data literacy and analysis are crucial for survival and growth in the cutthroat economy of today. The importance of data scientists to the success of contemporary businesses is directly related to its high demand. When it comes to making decisions, the most powerful firms in the world of data science career —Google, Apple, Amazon, and Facebook—all rely heavily on data. Skills Required to Learn Data Science From a Non-Technical Background Working as a Data scientist requires both Data science technical and soft skills. To work as a data scientist, one needs to possess the following abilities. Strong fundamental comprehension of mathematical ideas like probability and statistics Solid working knowledge of R or Python. Expertise in database management, including SQL and NoSQL technologies Experience with spreadsheets. Understanding of data visualization technologies like Tableau and Power BI. Solid comprehension of the principles of deep learning and machine learning Familiarity with cloud computing platforms such as GCP, AWS, or Azure A specialist in version control systems like GitHub and Git. Strong communication skills Data Analyst vs Data Scientist: What’s the Difference? S.No. Parameters Data Analyst Data Scientist 1 Definition To find useful insights, a data analyst looks at big data sets. A data scientist, on the other hand, is in charge of gathering, examining, and interpreting complicated data in order to develop prediction models and make judgments based on the data. 2 Career Scope A data analyst’s professional path usually begins with an entry-level job as a research assistant or data entry clerk. . A data scientist, on the other hand, is in charge of gathering, examining, and interpreting complicated data in order to develop prediction models and make judgments based on the data. 3 Eligibility A solid foundation in mathematics, statistics, and computer science, as well as competence with programming languages like Python and SQL, are typically prerequisites for becoming a data analyst. Additionally, data scientists need to be passionate about applying data-driven ways to solve challenging challenges and possess great communication abilities. 4 Course Duration Data analysts typically require a shorter educational path with an emphasis on basic data analysis skills. Data scientists typically require advanced degrees and deeper training in machine learning and complex statistical modeling, which results in longer course duration. 5 Demand Data Analyst has less capacity to solve more challenging issues and generate novel insights through sophisticated modeling. However, data scientists are often seen to be more in demand. 6 Top Company hiring Top organizations hiring for both professions include digital giants like Google, Amazon, and Microsoft, as well as companies in banking, healthcare, and retail sectors, Same as Data analyst, depending on the specific data demands. 7 Salary Making the appropriate decision may depend on your understanding of the income possibilities of a data science or analytics job. A data analyst makes, on average, $65,630 a year. Data scientists can earn up to $123,842 a year, according to Indeed. Step-by-Step RoadMap for Data science for Non-Technical Persons Step 1: Statistics and Probability The majority of recruiters want applicants with strong analytical skills when recruiting data scientists . You must cultivate mathematical intuition in order to acquire these abilities. Learn important statistics concepts including descriptive statistics and the normal distribution. Review the linear algebra ideas and calculus formulas that will subsequently aid in your comprehension of how machine learning algorithms are developed. Step 2: Proficiency in MS Excel Then start learning Excel. Excel is simple to learn and use thanks to its intuitive layout, even for people who are unfamiliar with data science principles. It is a great place to start when exploring and analyzing data, and it has powerful data cleansing, organizing, and manipulation tools, such as filtering, sorting, and removing duplicates. Discover important functions and formulas, such as text functions (LEFT, RIGHT, CONCATENATE), logical functions (IF, AND, OR), statistical functions (AVERAGE, MEDIAN, STANDARD DEVIATION), and lookup functions (VLOOKUP, INDEX MATCH). You should also learn how to handle missing values, eliminate duplicates, format data consistently, and identify trends with conditional formatting. Step 3: Working on Data with Power BI Data scientists have access to numerous sophisticated data visualization choices with Power BI. Among these features include smooth integration with other Microsoft products, such Excel and Azure, which facilitates team collaboration and dashboard sharing. With Power BI, you can create engaging data stories that can be used to reveal hidden trends, find correlations, or share findings with stakeholders. Next, investigate Power BI’s formula language, DAX, which allows you to perform calculations and modify data right within your visualizations. With DAX, you can build trustworthy data models that connect and manage connections between numerous data sources. Get even more inventive with the variety of visualization options available to tailor your findings for certain audiences. Want to Book A Free Expert Guidance Session? Book Now Get Free Career Counseling from Experts ! Email Phone Send Step 4: Start with Python Programming It is no coincidence that Python has emerged as the dominant language in data science. It is perfect for revealing hidden meanings in data because of its versatility, strength, and simplicity of usage. A diverse ecosystem of data science libraries, including scikit-learn, Pandas, and NumPy, provides pre-built tools for data manipulation, analysis, and machine learning. Gaining proficiency in Python programming opens up a wide range of career advancement opportunities and makes it simple to enter the data science field. Additionally, Python seamlessly integrates with other well-known data science tools, like Jupyter Notebooks and SQL databases, making the process more efficient. To begin, learn the fundamentals of Python, such as lists, tuples, and dictionaries, which form the basis for increasingly complex tasks. Next, look at Pandas, a helpful framework for data selection, cleaning, aggregation, and filtering. NumPy provides powerful tools for numerical operations and calculations on big datasets, including linear system solution and matrix multiplication. Lastly, try out visualization tools like Matplotlib and Seaborn to produce engaging data stories. Want to Book A Free Expert Guidance Session? Book Now Get Free Career Counseling from Experts ! Email Phone Send Step 5: Familiarity with Machine Learning Concepts Understanding machine learning concepts is necessary to build your toolbox because they make clear how algorithms utilize data to learn and create predictions. With this knowledge, you can create accurate forecasts, automate tasks, and glean valuable insights from raw statistics. Start by learning about supervised learning principles like regression and classification, as well as unsupervised learning ideas like clustering and dimensionality reduction. Discover model evaluation concepts like correctness, confusion matrices, and cross-validation. Once you have a solid foundation, move on to more intricate concepts like deep learning, reinforcement learning, and ensemble approaches. Step 6: Solidify your Data Management Skills Next, improve your knowledge of database administration and SQL (Structured Query Language), which will allow you to view, modify, and evaluate data in relational databases. Before analysis, data can be cleaned, modified, and filtered using SQL. Start by going over the foundations of SQL and database administration. Practice frequently on sites like LeetCode and HackerRank at the same time. With this two-pronged approach, you build a strong foundation and get closer to mastery. Step 7: Understanding Cloud Computing Platforms Data scientists are aware of the persistent challenges associated with managing constantly growing amounts of data, computationally demanding tasks, and the requirement for highly scalable resources. Thankfully, cloud computing provides a strong and adaptable substitute that can aid in resolving these issues. Cloud systems remove the limitations of on-premise hardware by enabling smooth resource scaling based on your project’s needs. The pay-as-you-go strategy is more economical since it eliminates the need for any up-front infrastructure expenditures. Start by considering familiarizing yourself with well-known cloud systems like Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Amazon Web Services (AWS), and Microsoft Azure. Your real-world experience will help you manage data sources and carry out essential tasks in cloud environments. Step 8: Experience with Version Control Systems You have to efficiently handle your code, scripts, and data as a data scientist. Working with others, keeping track of changes, and referring back to previous iterations when necessary all depend on version control systems like GitHub and Git. It’s important to maintain a detailed log of every modification you make to your code, data files, and scripts. This strategy encourages productive teamwork, enabling you to collaborate with colleagues in a fluid manner while integrating changes and averting conflicts. Learn the basic Git commands, including add, commit, push, pull, and merge, to get started. Examine further GitHub capabilities such as repositories, pull requests, branches, and version control visualisation. These resources can help you become a better team player and project manager. Step 9: Get to Work on Practical Projects This is your chance to demonstrate your abilities. Search for datasets in any field that piques your interest; the possibilities are nearly limitless, whether it be finance, music, sports, or another topic. Engage in real-world problem-solving initiatives since here is where learning by doing takes place. Finding and collecting the information required for investigation is essential before starting real-world initiatives. For this, a number of internet resources, including FiveThirtyEight, the UCI Machine Learning Repository, and Kaggle, can be helpful. By providing you with access to a range of datasets, these platforms enable you to work on pertinent projects that enhance your skills and expertise. Step 10: Networking and Collaboration There are many notable people in the data science community. Make connections with them both online and off through workshops, seminars, and a variety of online discussion boards. Think about collaborating on projects, exchanging experiences, and learning from others to hone your skills. Make the effort to set up and maintain your profile on well-known employment sites like Naukri and LinkedIn. Make sure you regularly add your relevant skills and accomplishments to your profiles. Participate on these venues by sharing your accomplishments, growth, and industry expertise. You increase your visibility to recruiters and your chances of being interviewed by doing this. S.No. Roles & Responsibilities Data Scientist Data Analyst 1 Data Focus: Data scientists frequently work with unstructured data and complicated challenges, finding novel ways to extract insights, data analysts mostly use structured data to answer particular questions. Analyze data, determine how to apply it to resolve problems, get vital information about a company’s customers, and boost sales. 2 Analysis Techniques: Data scientists use more sophisticated methods like machine learning, deep learning, and statistical modeling, data analysts use more straightforward statistical analysis and data visualization tools. Analytical and statistical techniques are used to analyze, clean, convert, and model data in order to do this. 3 Business Impact: Data scientists concentrate on creating predictive models to identify future opportunities and potential risks. Helps businesses make data-driven decisions that promote efficiency and growth by deciphering complex data and revealing hidden trends. 4 Dealing a data scientist employs advanced techniques like machine learning to develop predictive models and analyze massive, complicated datasets, Finding trends and patterns in current data is the main goal of a data analyst. 5 Tools Utilizing applications such as SQL and Excel to supply pertinent data for company choices You may use the correct data analysis tools to uncover the full picture of your data and then display it in a way that is suitable for stakeholders and members of your diverse professional network. Why Choose Data Science Training in Pune? Pune has become one of India’s major education and IT hubs. The city offers strong opportunities for learners looking to build careers in analytics, AI, and data science.so here the advantages of learning in Data science course near me Advantages of Learning Data Science in Pune Growing IT Ecosystem Pune has a strong presence of: IT companies Startups Analytics firms Product-based organizations This creates increasing demand for skilled data professionals. Industry-Oriented Training Programs Many institutes now provide: Live projects Hybrid learning Weekend batches Internship support Placement assistance These programs help beginners gain practical exposure instead of only theoretical knowledge. Better Networking Opportunities Offline and hybrid learning environments help students: Interact with mentors Collaborate on projects Build professional networks Participate in workshops and hackathons Data Science From a Non-Technical Background: FAQs 1. Can someone with a non-technical background work in data science? It is entirely possible for people with non-technical backgrounds to work in data science . Although it can be helpful, having a technical background is not required. Anyone can pursue a career in data science with commitment, self-education, and the acquisition of the required skills. 2. How will data science develop in the future? Data science has a bright future. The volume of data is growing, necessitating the analysis of knowledgeable people. Given the demand for data-savvy professionals across numerous industries, expect specialization in the field. Even while the phrase “data scientist” may evolve over time, the demand for insights based on data will only increase. 3. Can someone without any prior experience pursue a profession in data science? Without any prior expertise, it is feasible to work in data science. All that is required is a deep comprehension of the technologies and tools that data scientists use to build predictive models or help businesses use their data efficiently for forecasting the future. 4. How can I demonstrate my non-technical abilities to prospective data science employers? When moving into data science, it’s critical to emphasize your non-technical abilities. Highlight assignments or experiences in which you successfully applied abilities such as communication, critical thinking, problem-solving, and domain knowledge. Stress the importance of these qualities for data science projects and how they enhance your technical skills. 5. Does a job in data science require a degree in computer science or mathematics? Having a degree in mathematics or computer science is not necessary, but it can be helpful. When it comes to data science, skills and actual Global experience is highly prized. With this knowledge, you can create accurate forecasts, automate tasks, and glean valuable insights from raw statistics. Start by learning about supervised learning principles like regression and classification, as well as unsupervised learning ideas like clustering and dimensionality reduction. Discover model evaluation concepts like correctness, confusion matrices, and cross-validation. Once you have a solid foundation, move on to more intricate concepts like deep learning, reinforcement learning, and ensemble approaches. Step 6: Solidify your Data Management Skills Next, improve your knowledge of database administration and SQL (Structured Query Language), which will allow you to view, modify, and evaluate data in relational databases. Before analysis, data can be cleaned, modified, and filtered using SQL. Start by going over the foundations of SQL and database administration. Practice frequently on sites like LeetCode and HackerRank at the same time. With this two-pronged approach, you build a strong foundation and get closer to mastery. Step 7: Understanding Cloud Computing Platforms Data scientists are aware of the persistent challenges associated with managing constantly growing amounts of data, computationally demanding tasks, and the requirement for highly scalable resources. Thankfully, cloud computing provides a strong and adaptable substitute that can aid in resolving these issues. Cloud systems remove the limitations of on-premise hardware by enabling smooth resource scaling based on your project’s needs. The pay-as-you-go strategy is more economical since it eliminates the need for any up-front infrastructure expenditures. Start by considering familiarizing yourself with well-known cloud systems like Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Amazon Web Services (AWS), and Microsoft Azure. Your real-world experience will help you manage data sources and carry out essential tasks in cloud environments. Step 8: Experience with Version Control Systems You have to efficiently handle your code, scripts, and data as a data scientist. Working with others, keeping track of changes, and referring back to previous iterations when necessary all depend on version control systems like GitHub and Git. It’s important to maintain a detailed log of every modification you make to your code, data files, and scripts. This strategy encourages productive teamwork, enabling you to collaborate with colleagues in a fluid manner while integrating changes and averting conflicts. Learn the basic Git commands, including add, commit, push, pull, and merge, to get started. Examine further GitHub capabilities such as repositories, pull requests, branches, and version control visualisation. These resources can help you become a better team player and project manager. Search for datasets in any field that piques your interest; the possibilities are nearly limitless, whether it be finance, music, sports, or another topic. By providing you with access to a range of datasets, these platforms enable you to work on pertinent projects that enhance your skills and expertise. Make connections with them both online and off through workshops, seminars, and a variety of online discussion boards. Think about collaborating on projects, exchanging experiences, and learning from others to hone your skills. Table of Contents PriyankaS3ri March 18, 2025 6:33 pm AWS certifications are highly regarded credentials in the field of cloud computing, showcasing your expertise in Amazon Web Services technologies. These certifications have become crucial benchmarks for IT professionals, with many organizations actively seeking AWS-certified individuals to lead their cloud initiatives. The journey to AWS certification often raises a common question: “How long does it take to complete an AWS certification?” The answer varies for each individual and depends on several key factors: Previous cloud computing experience Chosen certification level Available study time Learning resources Individual learning pace This guide provides an overview of realistic timeframes for different AWS certifications, assisting you in planning your certification path effectively. You’ll find estimated study durations for various certification levels and discover strategies to optimize your preparation time. Remember: Your certification timeline is unique to you . Take into account your current knowledge, available time, and learning style when planning your AWS certification journey. Making a study plan that fits your objectives and unique situation is the key to success. Understanding AWS Certification Levels AWS divides its certifications into four levels, each of which is intended to verify a certain degree of expertise and understanding in cloud computing: 1. Foundational Level AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner Perfect for newcomers to AWS and cloud computing Discusses AWS services, security, cost, and fundamental cloud ideas. Ideal for non-technical roles needing cloud awareness 2. Associate Level Solutions Architect Developer SysOps Administrator Validates hands-on experience with AWS services Tests practical implementation skills Requires understanding of AWS architectural principles 3. Professional Level Solutions Architect Professional DevOps Engineer Professional Demonstrates advanced technical skills Tests complex solution design abilities Requires deep AWS expertise and real-world experience 4. Specialty Certifications Advanced Networking Security Machine Learning Data Analytics Database SAP on AWS Focuses on specific technical domains Validate expertise in particular AWS service areas For AWS professionals, a logical advancement path is created as each certification level builds upon the one before it. The requirements become increasingly rigorous as you advance through the levels, with professional and specialty certifications demanding substantial practical experience alongside theoretical knowledge. Estimated Study Durations for AWS Certifications Each AWS certification requires different time commitments based on its complexity and depth of knowledge required: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner 1-2 months of study 7 hours per week recommended Perfect entry point for beginners AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate 3-4 months of dedicated preparation 7-10 hours weekly study time Hands-on practice with AWS services essential AWS Certified Developer – Associate 2-3 months for experienced developers 3-4 months for those new to AWS Focus on coding and deployment practices AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional 5-6 months intensive preparation 10+ hours weekly commitment Requires a deep understanding of AWS architecture Previous AWS experience highly beneficial These timeframes assume consistent study habits and regular practice with AWS services. Your personal pace might vary based on your learning style, technical background, and available study time. Setting realistic milestones within these general timeframes helps track progress effectively. Factors Influencing Preparation Time for AWS Certifications The length of your AWS certification path is determined by a number of important variables that can either shorten or lengthen your preparation period: 1. Prior Experience with AWS Services Hands-on AWS experience can reduce study time by 40-60% Familiarity with cloud computing concepts speeds up theoretical learning Previous IT certifications provide a solid foundation for faster comprehension 2. Study Techniques and Learning Approach: Self-paced learning is flexible, but it necessitates a high level of self-control. Instructor-led training provides structured learning with expert guidance Boot camps deliver intensive, focused preparation in shorter timeframes Hybrid approaches integrate many techniques to maximize learning. 3. Quality and Variety of Study Resources Official AWS documentation serves as comprehensive reference material Structured learning is provided via video courses on websites like A Cloud Guru and Udemy. Practice exams help identify knowledge gaps and build exam confidence Hands-on labs provide practical experience with AWS services Study groups and discussion forums enable collaborative learning Each applicant has a distinct learning path created by the combination of these elements. A strategic selection of study methods and resources, aligned with your experience level, can significantly impact your certification timeline. Realistic Expectations for Different Candidates New Learners 3-4 months for AWS Cloud Practitioner certification Associate-level certificates take four to six months to get. Professional-level certificates take 8–12 months to get. Experienced Professionals 2-3 weeks for AWS Cloud Practitioner certification 4-8 weeks for Associate-level certifications 3-4 months for Professional-level certifications These timelines assume a consistent study schedule of 7-10 hours per week. Depending on your learning style and study time, your actual development may vary. Unlock the Secrets to a Powerful LinkedIn Profile ! Download Free e-Guide A cloud engineer with 2+ years of hands-on AWS experience can often prepare for the Solutions Architect Associate exam in just 2-3 weeks. The same certification might require 4-5 months for someone starting from scratch. The Security Specialty certification presents a unique case – cybersecurity professionals can typically prepare in 6-8 weeks, while those without security backgrounds might need 6-8 months of dedicated study time. Tips for Efficient Studying and Time Management Your road map to achieving your AWS certification is a well-organized study schedule. Here’s how to maximize your preparation time: 1. Create a Detailed Study Schedule Block specific time slots for study sessions Set weekly learning objectives Include buffer time for unexpected interruptions 2. Break Down the Exam Blueprint Allocating time according to domain weighting Mapping each domain to study materials Track progress through each section 3. Use Multiple Learning Resources Official AWS documentation Video courses from platforms like A Cloud Guru AWS Free Tier hands-on labs Practice exams from reliable suppliers 4. Implement Active Learning Techniques Take detailed notes during study sessions Create flashcards for key concepts Build mind maps for complex topics Explain concepts to others 5. Regular Progress Assessment Take practice exams every 2-3 weeks Review incorrect answers thoroughly Focus on weak areas identified in practice tests Maintain a score log to track improvement 6. Practical Application Set up real AWS projects Join study groups or discussion forums Participate in AWS workshops Connect with AWS communities on social media Your study environment matters too – designate a quiet space, eliminate distractions, and use productivity tools like time-tracking apps to maintain focus during study sessions. Depending on your background, level of commitment, and certification path of choice, the time commitment varies. Remember these key points for success: Set clear, measurable goals Select study materials based on your preferred method of learning. Practice hands-on with AWS services Take regular practice exams The path to AWS certification might take weeks or months, but the professional growth and career opportunities make it worthwhile. Start your journey today by evaluating your readiness and mapping out your personalized certification timeline. FAQs (Frequently Asked Questions) 1. What role does an AWS certification play in the cloud computing industry? AWS certifications increase your employability by proving your proficiency and understanding of cloud computing. They show that you can create, launch, and maintain apps on AWS, which is essential for companies using cloud computing. 2. What is the average preparation time for AWS certifications? The time required to complete AWS certification varies by individual but generally ranges from a few weeks to several months. Factors such as prior experience with AWS services, study methods, and the resources used can significantly influence preparation duration. 3. Which AWS certifications are available at what levels? AWS has four certification levels: Associate, Professional, Specialty, and Foundational. Each level caters to varying degrees of knowledge and experience, from beginners seeking a broad understanding to advanced professionals specializing in specific areas. 4. How long should one study for each level of AWS certification? Typically, candidates can expect to spend around 20-40 hours for the Foundational level certification, 60-80 hours for Associate-level certifications, and 80-120 hours for Professional-level certifications. The intricacy of specialty certificates might vary. 5. What factors influence the preparation time for AWS certifications? Preparation time can vary significantly based on several factors including prior experience with AWS services, chosen study methods (self-study vs. formal training), and the quality of resources used like books or online courses. 6. What tips can help optimize studying for AWS certifications? To optimize your study efforts, create a structured study plan with specific milestones. Regularly assess your knowledge through practice exams and adjust your study methods based on your progress to ensure efficient use of preparation time. old.content: Skip to content Home > How to Become a DevOps Engineer: Roadmap, Skills & Eligibility How to Become a DevOps Engineer: Roadmap, Skills & Eligibility Thinking about a career in DevOps? This blog walks you through the complete roadmap, essential skills, and who can get started. Whether you're a fresher or a working professional, DevOps Training in Pune can help you build a strong, future-ready tech career. Table of Contents PriyankaS3ri June 29, 2026 1:54 pm DevOps is at the center of the rapid change of the technology sector. DevOps techniques are being used by businesses all around the world to increase teamwork, decrease failures, and speed up software delivery. Choosing DevOps Training in Pune has become a wise career choice for both new hires and seasoned experts as the need for qualified workers rises. Whether you are starting from scratch or looking to upskill, this guide breaks down everything you need to know — from the DevOps roadmap to eligibility requirements. What Is DevOps and Why Does It Matter? Software development (Dev) and IT operations (Ops) are separated by the cultural and technical movement known as DevOps. Development and operations teams collaborate across the whole software lifecycle, from planning and coding to testing, deployment, and monitoring, as opposed to operating in separate silos. Want to Book A Free Expert Guidance Session?​ Book Now Get Free Career Counseling from Experts ! Email Phone Send The importance of DevOps cannot be overstated in today’s fast-paced digital world: Faster delivery: Software is released up to 200 times more frequently by companies that use DevOps strategies than by those that use traditional procedures. Higher reliability: Continuous testing and monitoring reduce system failures and downtime. Cost efficiency: Automation eliminates repetitive manual tasks, saving time and resources. Better collaboration: Shared goals and tools break down the communication barrier between teams. Competitive advantage: Businesses that ship faster and more reliably outperform their competitors. Global giants like Amazon, Netflix, and Google have scaled their operations precisely because DevOps principles are embedded in their engineering culture. With the DevOps Engineer salary in India ranging from ₹6 LPA for entry-level roles to ₹25+ LPA for senior positions, it is one of the most financially rewarding career paths in the tech industry today. Step-by-Step Guide to Becoming a DevOps Engineer Following a structured DevOps roadmap is the most effective way to build your career without feeling overwhelmed. Here is a step-by-step breakdown: Step 1: Build a Foundation in Linux and Networking Most DevOps tools run on Linux environments. Start with basic Linux commands, file management, shell scripting, and core networking concepts like DNS, TCP/IP, and HTTP. Step 2: Learn a Programming or Scripting Language Python, Bash, or Go are the most commonly used languages in DevOps workflows. Even basic scripting knowledge helps you automate repetitive tasks and write efficient pipelines. Step 3: Understand Version Control with Git Every DevOps team uses Git. To manage and work together on code, learn about branching techniques, merge requests, and platforms like GitHub or GitLab. Step 4: Master CI/CD Pipelines The core of DevOps is Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD).Build, test, and deployment processes can be automated with the use of tools like Jenkins, GitHub Actions, and GitLab CI. Step 5: Get Comfortable with Containers and Orchestration Learn Docker to containerize applications and Kubernetes to manage those containers at scale. These are non-negotiable skills for any modern DevOps role. Step 6: Examine Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Teams can provide and manage infrastructure using code using tools like Terraform and Ansible, creating environments that are uniform and repeatable. Step 7: Discover Cloud Platforms The most popular platforms are AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. Understanding cloud services, security, and cost management adds serious value to your profile. Unlock the Secrets to a Powerful LinkedIn Profile ! Download Free e-Guide Step 8: Pursue a DevOps Certification Earning a recognized DevOps certification — such as AWS Certified DevOps Engineer, CKA (Certified Kubernetes Administrator), or HashiCorp Terraform Associate — validates your expertise and increases your employability. Important DevOps Skills for a Successful Career It takes a combination of interpersonal skills and technical expertise to succeed in DevOps. Let us break both down. Technical Skills Required for DevOps Here is a concise comparison of the core DevOps tools and their purpose: Skill Area Tools/Technologies Why It Matters Version Control Git, GitHub, GitLab Tracks code changes and enables team collaboration CI/CD GitHub Actions and Jenkins Build, test, and deployment processes are automated. Containerization Docker, Podman Ensures consistent environments across systems Orchestration Kubernetes, Helm Manages containerized apps at scale IaC Terraform, Ansible Automates infrastructure provisioning Cloud AWS, Azure, GCP offers computer resources that are scalable. Monitoring Prometheus, Grafana, ELK Stack Tracks system health and application performance Scripting Python, Bash Automates repetitive operational tasks Mastery of these tools gives you a strong technical foundation to handle real-world DevOps challenges confidently. Soft Skills That Complement DevOps Expertise Technical skills alone will not take you far in a DevOps career. The role requires constant cross-functional collaboration, which makes soft skills equally important: Communication: You will regularly translate complex technical issues to non-technical stakeholders. Clear, concise communication prevents misunderstandings. Problem-solving mindset: DevOps engineers deal with production outages, pipeline failures, and security vulnerabilities. Staying calm and thinking analytically is essential. Adaptability: The tools and practices in DevOps evolve rapidly. Being open to continuous learning sets you apart. Collaboration: DevOps is fundamentally a team sport. Working well with developers, QA engineers, and product managers is critical. Ownership and accountability: Taking responsibility for the systems you manage builds trust across your organization. Eligibility for DevOps Training In Pune: Who Can Learn DevOps? DevOps’ inclusive learning path is one of its best features. DevOps courses in Pune are made to suit a broad spectrum of students, no matter what their background. Recent graduates and newcomers If you are a fresh graduate from a B.Tech, BCA, MCA, or BSc (IT/CS) program, you are well-positioned to start your DevOps journey. While prior industry experience is not required, a basic understanding of operating systems and programming is helpful. What freshers should focus on: Start with Linux fundamentals and Git Take up structured DevOps Training in Pune with hands-on lab sessions Work on personal projects using tools like Docker and Jenkins Aim for an entry-level DevOps certification to strengthen your resume Many institutes offering DevOps Classes in Pune provide placement assistance, mock interviews, and project-based learning specifically tailored for freshers entering the field. Working Professionals and Non-IT Learners You do not have to come from a software development background to pursue DevOps. Professionals from system administration, networking, QA testing, and even non-IT domains have successfully transitioned into DevOps roles. System admins and network engineers already understand infrastructure, making the shift to IaC and cloud tools intuitive. QA professionals benefit from their understanding of testing pipelines and automation frameworks. Non-IT professionals with strong analytical skills can upskill through dedicated DevOps programs with weekend or online batches. The key requirement across all profiles is curiosity and commitment to learning. With the right training environment, anyone can build a career in this space. Conclusion Modern software delivery is driven by a concept known as DevOps, which goes beyond a job description. By following a well-defined roadmap, building both technical and soft skills, and earning a recognized certification, you can unlock outstanding career opportunities across industries. Whether you are a fresher looking for your first break or a working professional aiming for a career switch, enrolling in 3RI Technologies DevOps Classes in Pune provides structured guidance, expert mentorship, and hands-on practice to help you succeed. There has never been a better opportunity to start your career in this in-demand industry, with income prospects getting better every year. Now is the ideal time to start building your technological future, so take the first step. This guide simplifies the most important concepts, making them easier to understand and apply. It's designed for students, professionals, and job seekers who want to build strong fundamentals before taking Cloud Computing Courses in Pune. Table of Contents PriyankaS3ri June 29, 2026 10:45 am Across many industries, cloud computing is now one of the most sought-after technologies. Whether you’re a student, IT professional, or someone planning a career switch, understanding important cloud computing terms is the first step toward building a strong foundation. If you’re planning to enroll in Cloud Computing Courses in Pune , knowing these terms will help you understand concepts faster and prepare for real-world cloud environments. This article breaks down the most important cloud computing concepts in simple language, so you can grasp the basics quickly and confidently move toward more advanced learning. Cloud: What Is It? The word “ cloud ” refers to a network of remote servers on the internet that manage, store, and process data instead of local servers or PCs. Rather than saving files on your laptop, you can store them securely online and access them anytime from any device with an internet connection. In simple words, the cloud acts like a virtual storage and computing environment where businesses and individuals can use technology without purchasing expensive hardware. Common Examples of Cloud Usage Saving photos to Google Photos Storing documents on Google Drive or OneDrive Streaming movies on Netflix Using Gmail for email communication Running business applications through Microsoft 365 Unlock the Secrets to a Powerful LinkedIn Profile ! Download Free e-Guide Multi-cloud, hybrid, private, and public clouds Cloud ecosystems are not the same. Depending on their operational, financial, and security needs, businesses use several deployment strategies. Cloud Type Ownership Description Best For Main Advantage Public Cloud owned and operated by an outside cloud service provider Services that are made available online are shared by several people. Startups, small businesses Low setup cost, Easy deployment, High scalability, Minimal maintenance Private Cloud owned and utilized by just one company Cloud infrastructure is exclusively used by one company. Banks, healthcare, government Enhanced privacy, Greater control, Better compliance, Improved customization Hybrid Cloud Shared ownership between the organization and cloud provider(s) integrates cloud environments from public and private sources. Large enterprises Better flexibility, Cost optimization, Improved business continuity, Easier workload balancing Multi-Cloud Managed across multiple third-party cloud providers Uses cloud services from two or more different cloud providers to run applications and store data. Enterprises seeking reliability, performance, and vendor flexibility Avoids vendor lock-in, improves resilience, and enables the use of best-in-class services from multiple providers What is Cloud Computing in Simple Terms The cloud computing meaning is straightforward: it is the delivery of computing resources over the internet whenever needed. Companies rent resources from cloud providers and only pay for what they use, as opposed to purchasing pricey servers. The on-demand provision of computer services, including as servers, storage, databases, networking, software, and analytics, via the internet is a basic description of cloud computing. Everyday Example Imagine watching a movie on Netflix. You don’t download the entire movie onto your computer. Instead, the content streams from cloud servers whenever you press Play. The same principle applies to cloud-based software, storage, and business applications.This model makes technology more affordable, flexible, and accessible for organizations of every size. Key Terms in Cloud Computing To truly understand the cloud ecosystem, you need to be familiar with some essential cloud computing terms. These are the most crucial ones that any novice should be aware of. Server: A server is a computer that offers files, programs, or services to other network-connected devices. Data Center: Thousands of servers that power cloud platforms are housed in a secure facility called a data center. Virtual Machine (VM): A virtual machine (VM) is a computer that runs on independent hardware and is powered by software. Storage: Cloud storage enables users to safely store data online and access them at any time. Scalability: Increasing or lowering computer resources in response to workload demand is referred to as scalability.. Elasticity: Elasticity automatically adjusts resources in real time based on traffic or application usage. IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service): Infrastructure as a Service, or IaaS, provides virtualized computer resources, including servers and storage, over the internet. Take Amazon EC2, for example. PaaS (Platform as a Service): Platform as a Service, or PaaS, allows developers to create, test, and launch applications without having to worry about maintaining the underlying infrastructure. Google App Engine is one example. SaaS (Software as a Service): Software as a Service, or SaaS, provides ready-to-use software programs online. Gmail and Zoom are two examples. Virtualization: Virtualization is the technology that allows several virtual machines to run on a single physical server. Backup: To guard against data loss from system malfunctions, cloud backup automatically saves copies of critical information. Disaster Recovery: Following unforeseen disasters, disaster recovery helps businesses to promptly restore systems and data. Latency: The amount of time that passes in cloud-based systems between a request and a response. Cloud Storage: Online space used to store data, accessible from anywhere. API (Application Programming Interface): The API (Application Programming Interface) facilitates communication between various software systems. Load Balancing: This technique distributes incoming traffic among multiple servers to ensure smooth operation. Whether you’re a student, an IT professional, or a business owner considering digital transformation, understanding these words is crucial because they form the basis of cloud computing services. Cloud Terminology and New Technologies As cloud computing evolves, new terms and technologies keep emerging. Staying updated with these trends is crucial, especially if you’re planning a long-term career in this field. Edge Computing: Data is processed closer to the point of generation (such as IoT devices) rather than only relying on centralized cloud servers. Serverless Computing: Enables code execution without the need for direct server management.The cloud provider takes care of infrastructure, scaling, and maintenance automatically. Containers and Kubernetes: Applications are portable between contexts thanks to containers, which bundle them with their dependencies. Kubernetes facilitates the effective management and orchestration of these containers. Multi-Cloud Strategy: utilizing several cloud service providers at once to increase dependability and prevent vendor lock-in. Cloud-Native Applications: Applications specifically designed to take full advantage of cloud environments, offering better scalability and resilience. DevOps and CI/CD: Practices that combine development and operations to enable faster, more reliable software releases through automated pipelines. Artificial Intelligence in the Cloud: Contemporary cloud platforms incorporate AI and machine learning services that assist companies in data analysis, process automation, and decision-making. Cloud Security: Cloud security encompasses best practices and technology intended to defend data, infrastructure, and cloud-based applications against online attacks. This blog explores popular DevOps job roles, salary expectations, required skills, and industry demand. Learn how DevOps training can help you transition into cloud, automation, and infrastructure-focused careers across leading organizations. Table of Contents PriyankaS3ri June 16, 2026 3:22 pm DevOps has emerged as one of the most popular job alternatives in recent years for students and working professionals in Pune, one of India’s largest IT hubs. The simple answer to the question of whether studying DevOps can lead to good careers is that it can—but only if you learn it properly. Let’s break down what DevOps really is, why companies want DevOps engineers, and how proper DevOps training in Pune can shape your career. What is DevOps and Why It’s in Demand DevOps is essentially a method of working where development and operations teams collaborate instead of operating independently. Instead of developers writing code and then “throwing it over the wall” to the operations team, both teams collaborate from start to finish using automation, monitoring, and continuous feedback. Why is it in demand? Simple—companies want to release software faster, with fewer bugs, and without downtime. DevOps makes that possible. Almost every IT company today, big or small, is either using DevOps practices or trying to adopt them. That’s why job listings for DevOps engineers, cloud engineers, and site reliability engineers keep increasing across Pune and other tech cities. A few reasons companies love DevOps: Faster software releases with fewer errors Quick fixing of bugs and issues Better teamwork between developers and operations staff More reliable systems with reduced downtime Teams spend more time creating new features than resolving issues that have existed for a while. This growing demand is also why there’s a real gap—more job openings than skilled people to fill them. That gap is your opportunity. How DevOps Training in Pune Helps You Get DevOps Job Opportunities Just knowing the theory of DevOps won’t get you a job. Recruiters want to see practical skills, hands-on project experience, and the confidence to handle real tools. This is where good DevOps training in Pune makes a real difference. A well-structured DevOps course should cover the full lifecycle—from version control and CI/CD pipelines to containers, orchestration, cloud platforms, and monitoring tools. For example, 3RI Technologies’ DevOps course in Pune is built around this exact lifecycle, with modules on Linux, AWS, Git, Jenkins, Docker, Kubernetes, Ansible, Terraform, and monitoring tools like Prometheus and Grafana. The course also includes live projects, such as building CI/CD pipelines using Jenkins, Docker, and Kubernetes, which gives students something real to show during interviews. What really matters for job opportunities is: Working on live projects, not just watching videos Getting exposure to industry-standard tools that companies actually use Mock interviews and resume-building support Guidance from trainers who have worked in the industry When your training includes all this, you walk into interviews with confidence because you’ve already “done the work” in a lab environment—not just read about it. Important DevOps Skills and DevOps Tools Needed for a DevOps Engineer Job To land a DevOps job, you need a mix of technical skills and tool knowledge. Here’s a simple breakdown: Core DevOps Skills: Basic Linux administration and shell scripting Understanding of cloud computing (especially AWS) Knowledge of CI/CD concepts Configuration management Containerization and orchestration Monitoring and troubleshooting Good communication and teamwork (since DevOps is all about collaboration) Want to Book A Free Expert Guidance Session?​ Book Now Get Free Career Counseling from Experts ! Email Phone Send Must-Know DevOps Tools: Tool Purpose Why It Matters Git/GitHub Version control Tracks code changes and team collaboration Jenkins CI/CD automation Build, test, and deployment are automated Docker Containerization Packages apps so they run anywhere Kubernetes Container orchestration Manages and scales containers Ansible Configuration management automates the setup of servers Terraform Code for Infrastructure Builds infrastructure using code Prometheus/Grafana Monitoring Tracks system performance AWS Cloud platform hosts and grows programs How to Get Better Job Opportunities with a DevOps Certification A DevOps certification acts like proof that you’ve actually learned and practiced these skills. While certificates alone don’t guarantee a job, they help in a few practical ways: When HR is reviewing hundreds of applications, they make your resume stand out. They show recruiters you’ve covered a structured syllabus, not just random YouTube videos Some certifications (like AWS Certified DevOps Engineer) are recognized globally and can open doors to better-paying roles They give you a confidence boost during technical interviews because you’ve already been tested on the concepts Think of certification as a door-opener—it gets you the interview call. How well you can describe your projects and use your abilities will determine what occurs next. Unlock the Secrets to a Powerful LinkedIn Profile ! Download Free e-Guide Understanding the DevOps Career Path After Completing a DevOps Course in Pune Once you finish your course, you don’t have to wait years to see growth. The DevOps course with placement is fairly fast compared to many other IT roles because the demand-supply gap is so wide. A typical path looks something like this: Entry-level roles : DevOps Engineer (Associate), Build and Release Engineer, Junior Cloud Engineer Mid-level roles : DevOps Engineer, Site Reliability Engineer (SRE), Automation Engineer Senior roles : Automation Architect, Release Manager, Security DevOps Engineer, DevOps Lead Here is a brief overview of common roles and their requirements: Role What You’ll Do Key Skills Needed DevOps Engineer Build and manage CI/CD pipelines, automate deployments Git, Jenkins, Docker, Kubernetes, scripting Site Reliability Engineer Keep systems stable and monitor performance Cloud platforms, monitoring tools, troubleshooting Automation Architect Design automation frameworks for infrastructure Terraform, Ansible, IaC concepts Release Manager Plan and coordinate software releases CI/CD knowledge, project coordination Security DevOps Engineer Add security checks into the DevOps pipeline Security tools, compliance knowledge The good thing about this path is that you don’t need to switch companies frequently to grow—many DevOps Engineers move into SRE or automation architect roles within the same organization after 2-3 years of solid experience. DevOps Salary and Career Growth for a DevOps Engineer in Pune Let’s talk numbers, because that’s usually what students want to know first. Salaries can vary based on your skills, the company, and how well you perform in interviews—but here’s a realistic range based on current trends in Pune’s IT market: Experience Level Approximate Salary Range (Pune) Fresher (0-1 year) ₹6-12 LPA 2-4 years experience ₹10-18 LPA 5+ years experience ₹18-30+ LPA Pune has a strong concentration of IT companies—from large firms like TCS, Infosys, and Wipro to mid-size companies and startups—all of which regularly hire for DevOps roles. The job postings for DevOps roles have been growing steadily, and companies are increasingly open to remote or hybrid arrangements too, which gives Pune-based professionals even more flexibility. The honest truth is that your starting salary depends heavily on how solid your hands-on skills are. Two students with the same certificate can get very different offers based on how well they can explain their projects, troubleshoot live issues, and communicate during interviews. Final Thoughts DevOps is not a “magic ticket” that guarantees a high-paying job overnight—but it is one of the most practical, in-demand skill sets in IT right now. If you put in the effort to actually understand the tools, work on real projects, and build your confidence through proper DevOps classes in Pune , the job opportunities are genuinely there. Pune’s IT ecosystem is large enough and growing fast enough to support fresh talent that’s willing to learn and adapt. The opportunity is real; the result depends on how you use your training. old.content: Skip to content Home > MySQL vs. PostgreSQL: Which Database Is Right for You? MySQL vs. PostgreSQL: Which Database Is Right for You? MySQL vs PostgreSQL – Which database is best in 2024? Compare performance, features & scalability before choosing! Table of Contents PriyankaS3ri March 20, 2025 1:19 pm Choosing the right database is one of the most critical decisions in software development, and the most common debate in the open-source world is mysql vs postgresql. While many developers weigh the mysql and postgresql differences, others come from a background in powerful enterprise solutions, often starting their journey with MS SQL Server Classes In Pune . Regardless of your starting point, understanding the fundamental difference between mysql and postgresql is vital for any tech professional. This guide will explore the postgre vs mysql comparison in detail to help you navigate the database landscape with confidence. Breaking Down the MySQL and PostgreSQL Differences In the world of databases, two of the most popular relational database management systems (RDBMS) are MySQL and PostgreSQL. Both are open-source, widely used, and powerful, yet they serve different use cases and offer distinct advantages. Choosing the right database for your application depends on factors like performance, scalability, features, and ease of use. In this blog, we will explore the key differences between MySQL and PostgreSQL, highlighting their strengths and weaknesses with real-time examples and scenarios. When it comes to database management in Data science and analytics courses in Pune , PostgreSQL and MySQL are two of the most popular choices, but their performance varies depending on project needs. PostgreSQL is preferred for complex queries, large datasets, and advanced analytics, making it highly relevant for learners exploring AI and data science courses . On the other hand, MySQL offers faster performance for simpler read-heavy applications, which is why it is widely used in web development projects. For students checking data science course eligibility or searching for a data science course near me , understanding the difference between PostgreSQL and MySQL can provide valuable insight into how real-world data is stored, managed, and analyzed. What is MySQL? MySQL is an open-source RDBMS that is widely known for its speed, simplicity, and reliability . It was originally developed by MySQL AB and later acquired by Oracle Corporation. MySQL is commonly used in web applications , such as WordPress, Joomla, and Drupal, because of its fast read performance and ease of integration. Real-Time Example: E-commerce Website Imagine you are developing an e-commerce website like Amazon. Since customers frequently perform searches, MySQL can efficiently handle high read operations with indexing . Many online stores rely on MySQL because it ensures fast retrieval of product listings while handling large volumes of transactions. What is PostgreSQL? PostgreSQL, also known as Postgres , is an advanced open-source RDBMS that is known for its extensibility, compliance with SQL standards, and support for complex queries . It is used in applications that require high data integrity, complex queries, and advanced features like JSON support and full-text search . Real-Time Example: Financial System Consider a banking system that requires transactional integrity and supports complex queries. PostgreSQL is an ideal choice because it offers ACID compliance , multi-version concurrency control (MVCC) , and support for stored procedures. A bank needs to ensure that transactions such as deposits and withdrawals are executed without data inconsistencies, making PostgreSQL a perfect fit. Key Differences Between MySQL and PostgreSQL Feature MySQL PostgreSQL Performance Faster for simple queries Optimized for complex queries SQL Compliance Partial SQL compliance Highly SQL-compliant Data Integrity Moderate High (ACID compliance by default) Scalability Horizontal scaling Vertical and horizontal scaling Extensibility Limited Highly extensible (supports custom data types and functions) JSON Support Basic JSON support Advanced JSON/JSONB support Replication Master-slave replication Multi-master replication Full-text Search Basic Advanced (supports GIN and GiST indexes) Concurrency Control Basic MVCC Advanced MVCC Usage Best for web apps, CMS, and e-commerce Best for complex applications, analytics, and financial systems 1. Performance Comparison MySQL is optimized for read-heavy operations and simple queries, while PostgreSQL performs better with write-heavy and complex queries . Scenario: Social Media Application MySQL: If you’re building a social media platform like Twitter, where users frequently fetch tweets, MySQL can efficiently handle these high-speed read operations. Breaking Down the MySQL and PostgreSQL Differences In the world of databases, two of the most popular relational database management systems (RDBMS) are MySQL and PostgreSQL. Both are open-source, widely used, and powerful, yet they serve different use cases and offer distinct advantages. Choosing the right database for your application depends on factors like performance, scalability, features, and ease of use. In this blog, we will explore the key differences between MySQL and PostgreSQL, highlighting their strengths and weaknesses with real-time examples and scenarios. When it comes to database management in Data science and analytics courses in Pune , PostgreSQL and MySQL are two of the most popular choices, but their performance varies depending on project needs. PostgreSQL is preferred for complex queries, large datasets, and advanced analytics, making it highly relevant for learners exploring AI and data science courses . On the other hand, MySQL offers faster performance for simpler read-heavy applications, which is why it is widely used in web development projects. What is MySQL? MySQL is an open-source RDBMS that is widely known for its speed, simplicity, and reliability . It was originally developed by MySQL AB and later acquired by Oracle Corporation. MySQL is commonly used in web applications , such as WordPress, Joomla, and Drupal, because of its fast read performance and ease of integration. Real-Time Example: E-commerce Website Imagine you are developing an e-commerce website like Amazon. Since customers frequently perform searches, MySQL can efficiently handle high read operations with indexing . Many online stores rely on MySQL because it ensures fast retrieval of product listings while handling large volumes of transactions. What is PostgreSQL? It is used in applications that require high data integrity, complex queries, and advanced features like JSON support and full-text search . Real-Time Example: Financial System Consider a banking system that requires transactional integrity and supports complex queries. PostgreSQL is an ideal choice because it offers ACID compliance , multi-version concurrency control (MVCC) , and support for stored procedures. A bank needs to ensure that transactions such as deposits and withdrawals are executed without data inconsistencies, making PostgreSQL a perfect fit. old.content: Skip to content Home > Serverless Computing on AWS: Concepts, Benefits, and Real-World Examples Serverless Computing on AWS: Concepts, Benefits, and Real-World Examples Learn how Serverless Computing on AWS simplifies modern application development with AWS Lambda, event-driven architecture, and EC2 automation. If you're exploring AWS Classes in Pune, this beginner-friendly guide will help you understand the core concepts, benefits, and real-world applications of serverless computing. Table of Contents PriyankaS3ri July 17, 2026 5:11 pm Cloud computing continues to evolve, and Serverless Computing on AWS is transforming the way modern applications are built. Instead of managing servers, scaling infrastructure, or handling maintenance, developers can focus entirely on writing code while AWS manages the backend infrastructure. In this blog, you’ll explore the concepts, benefits, and real-world examples of Serverless Computing on AWS, along with how services like AWS Lambda simplify application development. If you’re looking to build practical cloud skills through AWS Classes in Pune , understanding these concepts will help you create scalable, cost-effective, and efficient cloud applications. What is Serverless Computing on AWS? (Concepts and Benefits) To begin with, “serverless” does not imply the absence of servers. Servers still exist, but AWS takes full responsibility for provisioning, patching, and scaling them. As a developer, you simply upload your code, and AWS runs it whenever needed, then shuts it down automatically when it’s not in use. Imagine ordering dinner at a restaurant rather than preparing it at home. You don’t own the kitchen or buy the ingredients — you just place an order, and the meal is delivered. In conventional cloud computing, you rent a server and pay for it whether or not you make full use of it. With serverless computing , you pay only for the actual execution time of your code, which makes it attractive for students, startups, and businesses trying to minimise costs. Want to Book A Free Expert Guidance Session? Book Now Get Free Career Counseling from Experts ! Email Phone Send Serverless Computing versus Classical Computing Feature Traditional Computing Serverless Computing Server Management Manual setup and maintenance Fully managed by AWS Scaling Manual or pre-configured Automatic, based on demand Cost Model Pay for allocated resources Pay only for execution time Deployment Speed Slower, involves infrastructure setup Faster, code-focused deployment Idle Resource Cost Charged even when idle No charge when not running Ideal For Long-running, predictable workloads Event-driven, variable workloads Key benefits of serverless computing on AWS: Absence of infrastructure management—Developers just concentrate on writing logic. Automatic scaling that adjusts to traffic spikes without manual intervention. cost effectiveness since billing is determined by actual consumption rather than idle capacity. Faster time-to-market and built-in high availability across AWS zones. For students starting their cloud journey, these concepts are easier to grasp through structured, practical training. 3RI Technologies focuses on hands-on implementation of complete AWS projects from scratch , so learners actually build and deploy a serverless application themselves from day one. AWS Lambda Basics and Serverless Applications AWS Lambda is the backbone of serverless computing on AWS. To put it simply, Lambda allows you to execute code without the need for server provisioning or management. This is how it operates, step-by-step: A function is a brief segment of code that you write. You upload it to AWS Lambda. You define a trigger — a file upload, an API call, or a scheduled time. Lambda executes your code automatically whenever that trigger occurs, then shuts down. A serverless application is typically built by connecting multiple AWS services together, with Lambda acting as the “glue” that processes data and triggers actions. Python, Node.js, Java, Go, and other languages are supported by Lambda, and its functions can begin running in milliseconds. Practical example — photo-sharing app: A user uploads a photo to an Amazon S3 bucket. The upload instantly triggers an AWS Lambda function. Lambda automatically resizes the image into a thumbnail and a display size. The resized versions are saved back to S3, ready to show in the app. This shows the real value of Lambda: a task that would normally need a dedicated server running around the clock is instead handled in milliseconds, only when a photo is actually uploaded. Unlock the Secrets to a Powerful LinkedIn Profile ! Download Free e-Guide Reading documentation alone isn’t enough to grasp Lambda’s real potential—the concept clicks once you build something. This is how trainers at 3RI Technologies simplify Lambda basics: instead of explaining triggers and functions abstractly, they get students to write and deploy a real Lambda function in the first session, so a serverless application stops being theory and becomes something they’ve actually shipped. Event-Driven Architecture in AWS Serverless computing is built around event-driven architecture. Instead of applications running continuously and waiting for requests, they “wake up” only when a specific event occurs. An event could be A file being uploaded to Amazon S3. A new record added to a DynamoDB table. A user submitting a form through an API. A scheduled time trigger, like a daily report generation task. Picture a security camera system.
